subject.title: Feature: Session authentication PIN gate (framework-level tool blocking)

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in core session PIN gate, and what trusted verifier, secret storage, and reset semantics should define that boundary?
rationale: The code seam is clear, but the request changes core auth configuration, secret handling, session state, and prompt-injection defenses, so automation should not choose the product/security boundary.

options.title: Sponsor core PIN design
options.body: Define a narrow opt-in core feature with trusted TypeScript verification, secret redaction/storage rules, session reset semantics, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Route to plugin first
options.body: Ask for a plugin prototype using before_tool_call hooks and only expand core if that proves a missing core API or inconsistent security boundary.

options.title: Prefer broader step-up work
options.body: Decline a session PIN gate and instead fold the need into a broader trusted-device step-up authorization design for risky actions.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core PIN design
recommendation.body: Define a narrow opt-in core feature with trusted TypeScript verification, secret redaction/storage rules, session reset semantics, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the best available routing candidate from sampled auth/session history and security-sensitive CODEOWNERS context.
